thread.title: Site plan for Apple campus reveals who's been tapped for $1B project

author: Will Anderson
title: Site plan for Apple campus reveals who's been tapped for $1B project
text: – Managing Editor, Austin Business Journal Jan 3, 2019, 1:22pm CST A site plan application for the new Apple Inc. campus in Austin provides the first look at the team that will build it — and it's comprised of locals who already have experience working for the iPhone maker. The application for the 126.7-acre site was submitted Dec. 19 under the name Generational Commercial Properties, with no mention of Apple (Nasdaq: AAPL). But that's standard operating procedure for the technology giant, which likes to keep a low profile with its real estate deals. The address is given as 6800 W. Parmer Lane. Generational Commercial Properties is led by President Joe Llamas , who previously oversaw construction of Apple's nearby Americas Operations Center at 12545 Riata Vista Cir. when he was regional vice president for McShane Development Co. Other companies involved in the new Apple campus, which is expected to be a $1 billion investment and initially employ about 5,000 people, are civil engineering firm Garza EMC and Studio8 Architects Inc. Studio8 handled design of the Americas Operations Center. The application refers to a campus with 12 office buildings, amenity buildings and parking, plus the expected utility, drainage, grading, and landscape improvements. It also notes construction will be done in phases. The application seeks planned unit development zoning. Some other interesting tidbits: Much of the new Apple campus will be in the Rattan Creek Watershed — with water quality, water detention, drainage and other improvements planned — as well as the North Edwards Aquifer Recharge Zone. In addition, the north end of the site is within the Federal Emergency Management Agency's 100-year floodplain. Apple is in line to receive up to $25 million in taxpayer-funded grants from the Texas Enterprise Fund if it meets goals for capital investment and job creation. Williamson County commissioners have also approved a 65 percent property tax rebate for 15 years, as long as the company meets certain benchmarks. ATX Real Estate News has more on the players identified in the site plan application. – Managing Editor, Austin Business Journal Jan 3, 2019, 1:22pm CST Deadline: Wednesday, January 30, 2019 Best Real Estate Deals of 2018 Nominate for the 27th annual Best Real Estate Deals!
